text:
alice: Heads up — staging p95 latency jumped ~40% after we onboarded checkpoint x-3b-v2 a few hours ago. No config rollout besides that. Anyone seen this pattern?
ben: saw the alert. p50 barely moved, p95 and p99 up. Looks like long-tail batches.
carla: I pulled a profiler trace for a few requests around 1024 tokens. Kernel selection keeps falling back to generic_attn for the last ~200 tokens. Paste: 
```
carla: kernel_selector: model=x-3b-v2, seq_len=1024 -> chosen_kernel=generic_attn, rationale=fallback_mismatch
carla: p99 top: 42% generic_attn_compute, 18% copy_kv, 12% batch_sched_wait
```
carla: seems different from x-3b-v1 where cuda_attn_v2 was used for same seq distribution.
dan: interesting — did tokenizer change? If tokenization produces longer EOS or extra special tokens, seq_len distribution shifts and hits a different kernel path.
erin: CI perf job for the model onboarding flagged a regression in token-length histogram but it was marked as acceptable (small sample). ci-bot: `perf-checker: model x-3b-v2 / onboarding/perf — FAILED (p95 +36%)`
frank: I repro'd locally with the staging model and a sample prompt set. quick curl to staging reproduces: `curl -sS -H 'x-model: x-3b-v2' -d @sample_prompts.json https://staging.api.redwood` then run perf harness.
alice: good repro. Can we bisect between the two model artifacts? Maybe tokenizer vocab or model-config changed.
ben: diffing model package now. Found one change in model-config.json: "eos_behavior": "merge" vs old "eos_behavior": "append". That changes whether we append an explicit EOS token or merge with final token.
carla: that would shift tokenized lengths by +1 for many examples. Kernel selection logic has a sequence-length threshold table that picks specialized kernels for <=960 and <=512; bumping many queries over 960 could push them into fallback.
dan: quick experiment: I patched kernel-selector to treat <=1024 as eligibile for cuda_attn_v2 and ran perf. p95 dropped ~28% (not fully back to baseline but big win).
frank: we should NOT hot-fix kernel thresholds blindly — could break other models. Better: short-term rollback of the model onboarding to unblock staging, then add test coverage and a selector heuristic that uses recent seq_len histogram.
deploy-bot: rollout stopped for x-3b-v2 to staging at 2147654389 per manual stop request by alice :warning:
alice: filed rollback PR: #4219 — rolling staging back to x-3b-v1. Also filing a rollout blocker ticket and marking release-blocker.
erin: action items: 1) revert staging (alice / #4219), 2) eng-runtime to make selector adaptive (ben + dan), 3) add tokenizer-length regression test to onboarding CI (frank), 4) add perf-canary comparing kernel choices (carla).
ben: I'll open a PR for a conservative selector change that consults model metadata `preferred_kernel_profiles` and falls back to history-based decision.
carla: adding a perf test that runs 500 prompt samples and asserts p95 within 10% of baseline on onboarding CI. I'll add to the onboarding job.
ci-bot: perf job queued: `onboard-x-3b-v2 -> perf-smoke`
alice: thanks all. Once rollback is live I'll re-run the staging checks and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollback of x-3b-v2 to x-3b-v1 completed at 2147654555 (staging).
alice: staging p95 back to baseline after rollback. Closing immediate blocker. We still need the longer-term selector + CI guard.
dan: noted. I'll draft RFC for selector heuristics and include kernel safety nets.
frank: I'll add test vectors for tokenizer changes and a small regression harness.
erin: assigning tickets: RUNTIME-1123 (selector), RUNTIME-1124 (onboard CI perf), RUNTIME-1125 (canary/observability).
alice: perfect. Thanks team — great triage.
carla: leaving a pointer to the profiler trace and kernel logs in the incident doc.
frank: one more note: model packagers — please include a token-length histogram in model metadata to help automatic decisions.
alice: agreed, add to onboarding checklist.
